issues.finding: The fixture comment in tests/hook-wiring-parity.bats justifying `git init` is falsified by measurement. It states: '가드는 $FILE의 dirname에서 git root를 유도하므로 (F72) git이 아닌 임시 디렉터리는 root 해석에 실패해 fail-closed가 되고 deny 단언이 tautology가 된다.' I ran my full 116-case corpus twice against the HEAD guard — once in a `git init` temp repo and once in a plain non-git `mktemp -d` — and got 116/116 IDENTICAL verdicts (78 ALLOW / 38 DENY both times). Root-resolution failure never produces a deny: __root is consulted only in the `! -e $FILE` delete-then-recreate arm (guard:398-415), and record_guarded_edit's failure path (guard:471-474) only prints a warning and returns 0. The fixture works, but for a different reason than the one written down, and the `git init` is not load-bearing.
issues.why_it_matters: This is the third occurrence of the same defect class inside one feature — an assurance sentence asserted without measuring it — and it is in the very comment that was rewritten to fix the second occurrence (the auditor's F-2), a comment that itself says 'security-auditor가 실측해 지적했다'. The pattern, not this instance, is the problem.

issues.introduced_by: 96b862d (this feature, in response to round 1's issue #3)
issues.finding: The deny-reason assertion is not switch-specific, so it does not do what its comment claims ('deny 사유가 이 스위치를 지목하는지까지 단언한다'). The shared deny string embeds the literal 'disableCommandPluginSources' in its explanatory clause for ALL three switches. Measured: a plain disableAllHooks off->true deny prints '... 최상위 disableAllHooks 켜짐(off→true) — ... (특히 disableCommandPluginSources는 managed settings에서만 유효) ...', which satisfies `[[ $output == *"disableCommandPluginSources"* ]]`. The assertion still excludes a deny from a *different rule* (wiring denies do not contain the name), so it is not vacuous — but it cannot distinguish which kill switch fired, which is the discrimination the comment promises.
issues.suggested_fix: Assert on the switch-naming fragment instead, e.g. `[[ $output == *"최상위 disableCommandPluginSources 켜짐"* ]]`. Zero new surface, and it makes the assertion mean what the comment says.

issues.finding: The class-closure device never fires in CI. The schema locator is hardcoded to `/Users/*/.vscode*/extensions/...` (tests/hook-wiring-parity.bats:469) and .github/workflows/ci.yml runs `bats tests/` on ubuntu-latest, where that glob cannot match — so the completeness test always takes its explicit-skip path in CI. ES-3's expectation ('스키마가 또 다른 boolean을 추가하면 테스트가 실패해 등록을 강제한다') therefore holds only on a macOS developer machine that happens to have the VSCode extension installed. F75 itself is the proof: the gap was found by a local run, not by CI. This does not fail F75 (unchanged from the parent, and outside SC-4's approved blast radius) but it materially limits the guarantee INV-13 claims to enforce.
issues.note: Related datum: the installed schema advanced from 2.1.238 to 2.1.243 during this evaluation session and the hook-affecting set was still exactly the three covered keys — so coverage currently holds, unobserved by CI.

issues.finding: ES-1 has no in-repo pin — see the dedicated judgment in `es1_tradeoff_judgment` below. The property is currently held only by an out-of-band probe (round 1's and mine); nothing in the repository would notice if the explicit skip degenerated into a silent pass.

The fixture ledger pollution is fixed for the F75 fixture but the same class remains for run_guard. One full suite run appended 13 entries to progress/.guarded-edits, of which 9 are `settings.json` — issued because run_guard targets `$(pwd)/settings.json`, the real repository path. Root `settings.json` is not in protected-integrity.sh's PROTECTED_GLOBS, so those entries are never consumed either; they are the same unconsumable residue 92249bb removed for the fixture, at a different path. Zero new `.tmp` fixture-path entries appeared (the ledger still carries 67 from before the fix), so the F75-specific claim is honoured — but the commit message's flat 'zero new ledger entries' is true of the fixture, not of a suite run.

The OLD_R gate does not distinguish 'no wiring' from 'could not parse the file', so an unparseable settings.json on disk skips the kill-switch check for all three switches. Correctly recorded in INV-13 and correctly held outside SC-4's blast radius; a contract now exists at progress/contracts/sprint-62.json (F76, agreed:false). Confirmed the deferral is real and not merely promised. Note the follow-up feature F76 is not yet present in progress/feature_list.json — the change-request is still in flight.

Fail-closed value handling denies numeric `0` as 'on' (measured: absent->0 and false->0 both deny). This is the documented and intended 'false/부재만 off' rule applied consistently to all three switches, so it is not a defect — but it is over-blocking on a value most readers would call falsy, and INV-13's value discussion lists 1/"true"/"false" without mentioning 0. Worth a word in the doc so the next reader is not surprised.

es1_tradeoff_judgment.question: The implementer deliberately shipped no in-repo test pinning ES-1 ('explicit skip when the schema is absent'), arguing that the schema path is inline in the completeness test, that pinning it would require an injection point, and that the injection point would itself become a surface for switching the completeness check off — which is exactly what SC-2 protects.
es1_tradeoff_judgment.verdict: The conclusion is right; the premise is not. Do not require an injection point — but the inference that therefore no in-repo pin is possible is falsifiable, and I falsified it.
reasoning: The half that is correct: an env-var override (SCHEMA_OVERRIDE=/dev/null or similar) read by the production classifier would be a genuine bypass surface. Anything able to point the locator at an empty path can turn the class-closure device off from outside the file, and SC-2 exists precisely to keep that device un-narrowable. Rejecting that design is the right call.

The half that is wrong: pinning ES-1 does not require touching the classifier at all. I pinned it in this session with a purely out-of-band probe — a temp-dir `ls` shim that returns non-zero only for arguments containing 'claude-code-settings.schema.json', placed ahead on PATH for one nested bats invocation. The real test file ran unmodified and produced 'ok 7 ... # skip claude-code settings 스키마 없음' while the six F75 tests stayed green. Nothing in the guard or in the completeness test changed, so no bypass surface is created: the shim lives in the test's own temp directory and has no reachable effect on the production path.

That technique is directly repackageable as an in-repo @test: build the shim in BATS_TEST_TMPDIR, invoke `bats --filter '완전성'` on the real file with the shim on PATH, and assert the TAP line contains '# skip'. Cost is one nested bats run (~1s). It executes the real skip path rather than asserting about it.

A cheaper, weaker alternative also exists with zero new surface: a static meta-test asserting that the completeness test's source still contains its explicit `|| skip "..."` guard and contains no bare `return 0` fallback. That pins the shape ('explicit skip, not silent pass') without executing it — the same technique F45 already uses in this repo to cross-check is_protected() against INV-12.
es1_tradeoff_judgment.impact_on_this_judgment: ES-1 is met on the merits and I verified it by execution, so the missing pin does not fail the criterion. It is recorded as I-6 (low) and as a criteria gap: the durability of ES-1 currently rests on an evaluator remembering to re-probe it, which is precisely the kind of guarantee INV-14 says should be held by detection rather than by prediction.
es1_tradeoff_judgment.recommendation: Add the nested-bats shim test in the next iteration or fold it into the F76 contract. Do not add any override knob to the classifier.

missing_criteria: SC-3's textual scope is still 'docs/INVARIANTS.md INV-13 본문' only. Round 1 already logged this and the gap has now produced a third and fourth instance (I-1 in a test comment, I-3 in a code comment, I-4 in the contract's own evidence block). The next contract should scope reverse-consistency to *every* place the guarantee is stated: the invariant doc, code comments, user-visible deny strings, test-fixture rationale, and the contract's _implementation_evidence.

No criterion requires that an assurance sentence ship with the command that measured it. Every falsified claim in this feature (round 1's 'over-blocking only', the auditor's F-1 and F-2, and my I-1) was a plausible-sounding statement written from code reading. A criterion of the form 'each newly written guarantee sentence names the probe that established it' would have caught all four at authoring time.

No criterion covers CI reachability of an enforcement test. ES-3 assumes the completeness test will fail when the schema grows, but the test cannot run on the only platform CI uses (I-5). 'The enforcement point executes in CI, or its non-execution is an explicit, reviewed exemption' belongs in the next contract.
ambiguous_criteria: ES-1 says '기존 동작대로 명시적 skip' without stating how that is to be verified, which let the property be satisfied without being pinned. Round 1 flagged the same thing; it is still unaddressed.
criteria_gaps.action_required: None of these reverse this judgment. Fold the SC-3 scope widening and the 'name the probe' rule into the next critical-tier contract (F76/sprint-62 is the natural carrier, since it touches the same guard).

Both directions reproduced, so INV-13's corrected bidirectional sentence now matches the code. lessons_for_calibration: Three independent reviews of one small change each found at least one assurance sentence that measurement contradicts — and each correction introduced the next one. The failure is not any single sentence; it is writing rationale in the same pass as code and never running the claim. The cheap structural fix is to require that a guarantee sentence cite the probe that produced it.

A shared deny string that names one switch inside a general explanatory clause silently defeats per-switch output assertions. When a message is shared across a set, assert on the part that varies, not on the part that is always present.
